headline: Expedia has still not said whether customer data was taken or which vendor was breached.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read Skift (s001): still Expedia's Nov 12 statement, no update. Expedia Group's newsroom and investor news pages were not checked: access blocked (HTTP 403). No new Expedia statement, customer notice or state attorney-general filing found (the Maine AG portal returned 403; not checked: access blocked). A Nov 19 KARE 11 story syndicated by Valley News Live repeats Expedia's statement and the group's claims; not independent. Mid-November Qubole coverage (SecurityWeek, CSO Online) restates Wiz and Sentra (s004, s005); nothing new on Expedia. q003 (data taken) and q004 (which vendor) stay open. No new rumors. Staleness check done: head still true. Not yet eligible for resolved: last update u004 is Nov 22.
author: Research agent

headline: A second outlet describes the group's posted Expedia files: hundreds of thousands of emails, possibly old; still not confirmed by Expedia.
summary: New source: Cyber Daily (s008, Tier 2, Nov 12 Australian time), independent of Cybernews. It dates the group's leak post to Nov 3 (new timeline row t005), quotes the same claimed figures and says the posted extract lists hundreds of thousands of email addresses linked to travel data, some seen in earlier breaches, possibly historical. Added to c003, c004 (still Unverified: two outlets relay the group's claim but nobody has checked it) and c005 (still Reported: the files are not confirmed as Expedia's). No label change on any claim or the main question. Checked: no Expedia newsroom post or customer notice; no Form 8-K with Item 1.05 on EDGAR (latest 8-K Nov 4, earnings); no Qubole or Idera statement; no new Expedia statement since Nov 18. Staleness check done: head, known, not known, figures and size still accurate. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters, plaintiffs or contacts named. The group's page was not visited.
author: Research agent

headline: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm vendor incidents after the group behind the Expedia claim listed them; Expedia's vendor is still unnamed.
summary: New sources: Wiz (s004, Tier 3) and Sentra (s005, Tier 3) write-ups of the Oct 14 to 26 Qubole attack, now cited directly in c008 (still Reported; neither names Expedia), and BleepingComputer Nov 20 (s006, Tier 2). Added c011, n0n's claim that it carried out the Qubole attack (Reported; via Wiz's Nov 11 note and BleepingComputer), and c012, JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirming incidents at third-party providers after the group listed them (Reported; one outlet; no provider named, not tied to Expedia). c007 and c009 details refreshed. No label change on any claim or the main question. headline: Expedia confirmed attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider; a group claims a billion records.
summary: First build from Skift (Tier 2; partly behind a subscription) and Cybernews and The Seattle Times (all Tier 2, read Nov 22). c001 vendor attack Confirmed on Expedia's own statement to Skift and to The Seattle Times; no company page was found. c003, c005, c008, c009 Reported; c004 the billion-record claim Unverified; c006 whether customer data was taken and c007 vendor and method Not established. A larger figure of over 1TB in the sweep notes was not in either source and was dropped. The group's leak page was not visited. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters or contacts named.
